GetScaledAmountForMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only. ShouldScaleInMultiplayer / GetScaledAmountForMultiplayer feed PowerCmd.Apply's MultiplayerScalingModel leg (PowerCmd.cs:128-131), waived as step 14 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json.

AfterAttack.issue: C#'s hook is AfterAttack, which fires ONCE per AttackCommand after every hit has landed (SkittishPower.cs:56-69 searches command.Results for a DamageResult whose Receiver is the owner); the sim uses on_damage_received, which fires PER HIT. The once-per-turn gate makes the totals agree, but the TIMING does not: the sim grants the block after the first qualifying hit, so the second and later hits of a multi-hit Attack card are absorbed by block the game has not granted yet. Identical shape to power/curl_up's, whose C# also defers to the end of the card play, and reachable the same way -- the ported Phantasmal Gardener plus any multi-hit Attack. The sim does have the AfterAttack slot available: hooks.py:361-370 after_attack, used by VigorPower and GigantificationPower. Third-file citations, not hashed here. LIVE 2026-07-29 (round 11): unlike power/curl_up (whose sibling gap this same paragraph analogizes to and which turned out to have been fixed already, see that record), SkittishPower here is still exactly the pre-fix shape -- `on_damage_received` at today's powers.py:2136-2157 grants the block on the first qualifying hit, with no card-play latch. EXECUTED: enemy with Skittish 8, hit by a Twin Strike (2x5 unpowered-relative attack, both hits normally unblocked) -- `enemy.hp` drops by only 5 (not 10) and `enemy.block` ends at 3 (8 granted after hit 1, then 5 absorbed from hit 2), because the sim grants block mid-card. The ported Phantasmal Gardener (monsters/underdocks/phantasmal_gardener.py:50, `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, SkittishPower, ...)`) is a reachable elite encounter (`PHANTASMAL_GARDENERS_ELITE`, monsters/underdocks/__init__.py) and Twin Strike is an ordinary starter-adjacent Attack card, so any player using a multi-hit Attack against this elite under-deals damage relative to the game by exactly the amount of block granted mid-swing.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE SLOT HALF IS CLOSED: the reset is now `after_player_turn_end` (powers.py:1927), the sim's Hook.AfterTurnEnd slot (combat.py:809 / CombatManager.cs:1307). WHAT REMAINS is the side test: SkittishPower.cs:73 acts only when `side != base.Owner.Side`, while powers.py:1927-1929 resets on every player turn end regardless of the owner's side. For an enemy-owned Skittish -- the only ported case, the Phantasmal Gardener -- the two agree; a player-owned one would reset at the wrong side's end. Dormant, unchanged. DORMANT, re-confirmed 2026-07-29 (round 11) by enumeration: `grep -rln SkittishPower --include=*.py sts2_rl/ | grep -v powers.py` returns exactly one file, `monsters/underdocks/phantasmal_gardener.py`, and its only application is a self-apply (`PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, SkittishPower, ...)`, owner = the enemy). No card, relic, potion or event grants SkittishPower anywhere in sts2_rl/ (same grep across cards/relics/potions returns nothing), so a player-owned Skittish -- the only shape that could expose the missing side test -- does not exist in ported content. Trigger: porting any future player-side SkittishPower source.

guards.rationale: powers.py:1810 `ValueProp.MOVE in props`. Identical -- and note this is the weaker Move test, NOT IsPoweredAttack, so an UNPOWERED Move (a status card damaging the player) does qualify on both sides. The sim gets the distinction right where power/thorns and power/curl_up drop their gates entirely.
powers.py:1809 `card is not None`. Identical: only card attacks trigger Skittish, not monster moves or powers.
powers.py:1811 `amount > 0`; the sim's amount is the post-block unblocked loss (cmds.py:122). C#'s `!= 0` and the sim's `> 0` agree because unblocked damage is never negative.
powers.py:1808 `not self._blocked_this_turn`, set at :1814 before the block gain exactly as C# sets its flag at :63 before its GainBlock.
powers.py:1816-1818 passes `props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED` explicitly. One of the eight powers that get this right.

powers.py:1812. C# reaches AfterAttack only through the attack pipeline and would gain block on a dying creature; the sim's guard is defensive and cannot produce a divergence, because block on a dead creature is discarded either way.
